title: tetragonanthus elatus
intro: Tetragonanthus elatus, commonly known as the African walnut, is a plant species within the Annonaceae family. It is traditionally used in West African medicine, valued for its potential health benefits, which include aiding in the management of fever, malaria, and respiratory issues, as well as providing antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Tetragonanthus elatus are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include alkaloids, glycosides, and flavonoids, that have been shown to possess antimicrobial and antiviral activities. Furthermore, research suggests that the plant's bioactive compounds may also exhibit hepatoprotective, cardiovascular protective, and neuroprotective properties, although more studies are needed to confirm its full range of effects.
